title: pfcfg parse-tree bundle
description: Structural mirror of pfcfg/model.py's parse tree, self-contained per entry config. Validates document shape only - last-writer-wins, @include_once dedup, @ifdef/@ifndef truthiness, and interpolation resolution are evaluator behavior over this shape, not something this schema can check statically. See solution/schema/design-note.md.

entry.description: Key into `files` for the entry config (mirrors model.MergedConfig.entry / model.ParsedFile.path).

files.description: Every file reachable from `entry` via @include/@include_once, keyed by resolved_path.

path.description: Dotted section path (model.SectionHeader.path). Pointer-setting, not a container - does not nest keys.

key.description: Bare key, joined with the walk's current section pointer at eval time - not a dotted path (model.KeyAssignment.key).

value.description: Parsed via interpolate.py's _ValueParser, unresolved. Empty array = empty string value. Always an array, even for values with zero interpolation - no bare-string shortcut, no comma-list splitting.

target.description: Literal directive path text, relative to its file (model.Include.target). Unresolved, kept for round-trip display.

once.description: true for @include_once, false for @include. Whether it actually dedups is walk-scoped evaluator state (a seen-set shared across the whole bundle), not something this flag alone determines.

resolved_path.description: Static join-and-normalize of target against its containing file's directory, computed once at conversion time (same as walker.py's os.path.realpath(os.path.join(base_dir, target))). Key into `files`.

var.description: Guard variable name, looked up against the evaluation environment (never resolved here).

body.description: Gated nodes, in source order. May contain Section/Assign/Include/Conditional nodes, including further nesting - no type-level restriction on what a conditional can gate.

var.description: ${VAR...}. Cannot contain '}' or ':' - the parser's var-name scan stops at the first occurrence of either, so this is a structural fact, not an invented restriction.

expr.description: The :- (default) or :+ (alt) sub-expression, itself a segment sequence (recursive - handles nested ${...}/$(...)). Absent iff mode is "plain".

path.description: $(section.key) target. Not pattern-restricted to dotted identifiers - the reference parser (_parse_key_ref) accepts any text up to the closing ')' with no charset check, so this schema doesn't invent one either.

Line.description: 1-indexed source line (model.SourceLoc.line), for diagnostics parity with the reference evaluator.
